record.original_question: What is the group-theoretic and topological mechanism of vanishing for Nambu micro-graphs and their linear combinations?

evidence.quote: To reveal this mechanism in full is a standing problem; the impact of topology (in Γ) on arithmetic (in φ(Γ)) will make possible the study of d ≳ 5, so far costly.
What is the group-theoretic and topological mechanism of vanishing for Nambu micro-graphs and their linear combinations ?

artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph cocycles and Nambu-Poisson structures
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 2$ and consider a smooth manifold $M^d$ equipped with a Nambu–Poisson structure of rank $d$, i.e. a multilinear bracket $\{\,\cdot\,,\dots,\cdot\,\}\colon C^\infty(M)^{\otimes d} \to C^\infty(M)$ given (in coordinates) by a Jacobian determinant against a top-degree multivector and a fixed volume form. Following Kontsevich's graph calculus, to every finite directed graph $\Gamma$ on $n$ aerial vertices and a fixed number of ground vertices (with appropriate edge-labelings and signs) one associates a polydifferential operator $\Gamma \mapsto \mathcal{O}_\Gamma$ acting on tuples of smooth functions, where each aerial vertex carries a copy of the Nambu multivector and each edge represents a partial derivative landing on the function/multivector at its target. A "Nambu micro-graph" is a connected component appearing in the expansion of such an operator after one decomposes each Jacobian-determinant vertex into its $d!$ signed permutation summands; the resulting operator $\varphi(\Gamma)$ is a sum of differential monomials indexed by these micro-graphs.

A formal $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination $\sum_i c_i\, \Gamma_i$ of such (micro-)graphs is said to vanish on Nambu–Poisson structures if $\sum_i c_i\, \mathcal{O}_{\Gamma_i} \equiv 0$ as a polydifferential operator on $C^\infty(M)$ for every Nambu–Poisson structure of rank $d$ on every smooth $d$-manifold $M$.

Problem. Identify and characterize, intrinsically and combinatorially, the group-theoretic and topological mechanism responsible for such vanishing. Concretely:

(a) Determine which subgroups of the symmetric/automorphism groups acting on the edge- and vertex-labels of $\Gamma$ (e.g. edge swaps at each aerial vertex generating signed actions through the Jacobian antisymmetrization) force the associated operator $\varphi(\Gamma)$ to be identically zero, and describe the resulting kernel of the map $\varphi$ on the space of (formal $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combinations of) Nambu micro-graphs.

(b) Identify the topological invariants of the underlying graph (such as Euler characteristic, cycle rank, planarity/embedding type, or higher topology of associated CW or moduli structures) whose values force or obstruct vanishing of $\varphi\bigl(\sum_i c_i \Gamma_i\bigr)$.

(c) Combine (a) and (b) into a structural description of $\ker \varphi$ valid for all dimensions $d \geq 2$, suitable for explicit computations of Kontsevich-type graph cocycles acting on Nambu–Poisson brackets in dimensions $d \gtrsim 5$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly posed as an open standing problem in the source preprint (November 2025), with no published resolution found. Web searches do not turn up any solution; it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Kontsevich–Nambu micro-graphs in dimensions d≥2 and Kontsevich's tetrahedral graph cocycle action.
status_evidence.claim: The paper poses the vanishing mechanism for Nambu micro-graphs as an open problem.
